content.rationale:
The commitment: `deccy drafts` is one read-only verb. Invoked bare, it scans the registry under `.deccy/work/` and returns one line per record carrying the record's handle, its state, and the workspace it names by name and path; an open record whose named workspace is not among the names jj reports is marked `drifted`, while a landed record's line never changes with its workspace's existence. `src/verb_drafts.rs` is that commitment as Rust, and nothing it does creates, rewrites, drops or forgets a record or a workspace.

The surface is nzrnrlky's and the route's. nzrnrlky fixes one lowercase verb, `drafts`, declaring no arguments in v1, whose bare call lists exactly the registry's records and reports drift per record; the handler is therefore `pub fn run(&Context, &[String]) -> Result<Vec<String>, Refusal>`, ynvwvzrm's row shape, and `HELP` is the verb's own line. qtqnuqxo orders the surface before the workspace: `--help` is answered first, from any context including a root-less one, and any other argument is refused naming that argument before `context.state()`, `draft_registry::scan` or `jj_workspace::list` is reached, so a refusal that names the argument cannot have come from the absent workspace. xlvoxmyl requires `--help` for every verb and rwlywqrk puts it under the same human-readable conventions as normal output: the text is one line introduced by the verb's own name, `deccy drafts`. utrzvyyt fixes the return — the handler returns its lines and writes no stream — and popowxnw fixes the failure: `Refusal::new(...)` with the offending word or path attached as evidence, never an exit and never a panic.

The listing set is the registry's scan, not the node space. rroqqrzq's `scan` returns every `.json` document under the root keyed by the handle its filename gives, and returns no records when the directory is absent; ntypuupx makes that scan refuse a document that does not conform to `schemas/work.json` or whose `handle` disagrees with its filename, naming the record, rather than surfacing or silently skipping it. The verb therefore turns the scan's `Error` — whose `Display` names the path it refused — into a `Refusal`, and lists exactly what the scan returns, landed records included, because vkkwusty's retention keeps them in the same directory. The root handed to the scan is `.deccy/work` under the store's root: rroqqrzq is handed the registry directory and derives nothing, so the derivation belongs to the verb, and the path is the one rroqqrzq and ntypuupx name; the store is opened on the trunk state root, never on the invocation workspace (M-TWO-ROOTS, lotlstzr), and zttrwlts's `context.state()` supplies it and already refuses a root-less context with the `no workspace` refusal popowxnw renders.

Each row is nzrnrlky's references and vkkwusty's state. nzrnrlky fixes that a row reports the handle, the state and the workspace by name and path, and that the handle is the key while the node, edit and workspace are references; qspsyqlp states the same listing as a requirement over every record. The row is `<handle> <state> <workspace name> <workspace path>`, taken from the scanned document (the registry has already checked its shape), so two records naming one node remain two rows with different handles, and the workspace path is not re-rendered through `Path` — the record's own string is what the line carries. vkkwusty supplies the two values: `open` is the record of a draft that has not landed and `landed` the record of one that has; the verb reads `open` as that fact and adds no third category.

Drift is vuopwuyo and yozqornv applied to the listing. jj owns whether a workspace exists and the registry owns the record's meaning, so the verb asks jj through tyoypkmp's `list` and compares the workspace name the record carries with the names jj reports; nzrnrlky leaves the jj invocation and the name/path matching open, and the landed module's list is exactly those names. An `open` record whose name is not in that list is marked drifted, because the record asserts a draft held in a workspace jj no longer has; a `landed` record is never marked, because no draft is written there any more and the retained record outlives its workspace by design (vuopwuyo, vkkwusty). The drift marker is appended to the open row and nothing else in the line depends on the workspace's existence, so a landed record's line is identical whether its workspace is present, absent or forgotten. The report is per record, not a summary (nzrnrlky, qspsyqlp), and a jj read failure is carried as a `Refusal` from tyoypkmp's `WorkspaceError`, its stderr or spawn reason preserved rather than read as an empty listing.

The verb only reads. `draft_registry::scan` and `jj_workspace::list` are reads, and the verb itself performs no write and no repair: it does not create the missing workspace, does not rewrite or drop the drifted record, does not delete a landed one, and leaves `nodes/` untouched. That is vuopwuyo's and yozqornv's stance — the report is the whole effect, and restoring either side would erase the difference being reported — and vkkwusty's retention is why the landed record is never a candidate for removal. Because nothing mutates, the verb is not an operation and carries no marker or undo.

The module is one flat file, `src/verb_drafts.rs` (szmuyqrq), using only `crate::context`, `crate::draft_registry`, `crate::jj_workspace`, `crate::refusal` and serde_json's `Value`; its gate is the self-contained test crate under `tests/verb_drafts/` that pulls the module and its siblings in through `#[path]` shims (knqkxzns).

The registry the verb reads is the repository's one registry. A repository has one `.deccy/work/`, in the trunk working copy whose root holds the store root (M-TWO-ROOTS, lotlstzr); a linked workspace (`jj workspace add`) is another checkout of that same repository, not a second registry, so the listing scans the store's root and never the invocation workspace's own tree (mrwtusss). That is also why an invocation there answers rather than refusing: mrwtusss confines the non-trunk refusal to invocations that write graph state, and `drafts` writes nothing — the listing is the whole effect — so it keeps working outside the trunk and lists the trunk's records, even when the linked tree holds a `.deccy/work/` of its own. The drift check is unchanged by that swap: the row is still built from the scanned document and compared against tyoypkmp's `list` for the invocation's jj, and the report still marks only an open record whose name jj does not have (vuopwuyo, yozqornv).
